conviction_note: The issuer's own calendar confirms H1 FY27 results on 18 Nov 2026 at 07:00, and nothing of the half beyond revenue to July (+4.6%) has been pre-released, so the numbers, the net debt and the first covenant test back at original levels (Sept 2026) are all new. That makes the scale large (abs 8% on a thin, highly geared equity: about £64m market cap against £159m net debt). The direction is close to balanced: FY27 PBT was already pushed to the low end on 10 Sep and the stock has fallen ~27% since late August; counterparty ProService and peer Vp read mildly positive for the contract and water book, while the Oct construction PMI (43.6) and the H2-weighted plan argue for a trim. So p_up is 46 and the scaled number -0.64 sits close to the findings sum of -0.7.

findings.finding: Speedy's FY27 profit guide rests on a second-half weighting (AGM, 10 Sep 2026), and the UK construction PMI then fell to 43.6 in October 2026 from 46.1, the sharpest contraction since June, with housebuilding at 35.1. A further trim of the H2-dependent outlook at the interims is therefore more likely than a firming.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Outlook cuts in trading updates moved the stock -18.06% (2024-01-30), -28.36% (2025-02-03) and -12.0% (2026-04-02). The 10 Sep 2026 low-end PBT guide moved it about -1.9% on the day (15.7p from 16.0p, Yahoo tape). The Nov 2025 half-year with a reiterated outlook moved +6.72%.
findings.why_not_priced: The low-end PBT guide is priced: the stock is down ~27% since late August. The October PMI came out on 5 Nov, and the share price since then (13.48p on 5 Nov to 13.72p) shows no reaction, so the macro deterioration has not visibly been translated into this name. This is still a macro-to-company transmission that the company has not confirmed, so it is sized small.

findings.finding: The direct counterparty ProService (8 Sep 2026) says it is 'performing ahead of management expectations, supported by the growth in Speedy Customer Solutions revenue streams', with FY27 revenue up ~20% y/y. That supports Speedy's £50-55m annualised revenue from the Commercial Agreement landing in the H1 numbers.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The ProService deal announcement and completion (6 Oct / 17 Nov 2025) coincided with +3.7% on 17 Nov 2025 and +6.72% at the Nov 2025 interims. The channel has not surprised separately since.
findings.why_not_priced: It is partly priced. Speedy's own AGM statement two days later called ProService trading 'encouraging' with conversion 'within the agreed range', and the stock fell after it. The counterparty's 'ahead of expectations' wording sits on an AIM microcap that few Speedy holders read, so a small residual remains. If it were priced, the 10 Sep statement would have held the price and it did not.
findings.independence: Speedy AGM statement, 10 Sep 2026, 'initial trading from our Commercial Agreement with ProService has been encouraging': https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/speedy-hire--sdy/agm-statement/9764248

findings.finding: Peer Vp plc (12 Oct 2026) reported a resilient H1 to 30 Sep 2026 and is on track for FY expectations, with 'encouraging momentum in water as AMP8 activity has grown in the second quarter' and strong electricity transmission. General construction (Brandon Hire Station) remains challenged. Speedy's mix has moved to national, regulated and infrastructure contracts, including a Thames Water contract.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed Speedy reaction to Vp read-across. Speedy's own H1 results moved -4.9% (2023), -4.14% (2024) and +6.72% (2025).
findings.why_not_priced: Speedy fell from 14.84p (2 Oct) to 12.74p (27 Oct) after the Vp update, so the market did not carry the peer's resilient H1 across. The link is real but partial: Speedy's regional and local general-hire base resembles Brandon (challenged) as much as Vp's specialist businesses, so the finding is sized net of that.
findings.independence: Speedy FY26 results name the Thames Water long-term contract and the exposure to regulated and infrastructure markets: https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/speedy-hire--sdy/final-results/9621791

findings.finding: The H1 balance sheet is the first covenant test back at original levels: the leverage test reverts at Sept 2026 after pre-year-end amendments. FY26 leverage was 3.3x, the auditor flagged a material uncertainty over going concern, and the AGM said leverage still runs at the top of the RCF ratchet with interest above expectations. Net debt (£159m) is ~2.5x the equity value, so the interim covenant and going-concern disclosure is a geared binary that leans slightly negative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: April 2025's 'Trading Update and Refinancing' moved +6.21%, and the stock rallied when debt risk was resolved. The 2 Apr 2026 update with net debt at £159m and slower deleveraging moved -12.0%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: a market cap of ~£64m against £159m net debt is the market's own discount for exactly this. What is not known is the Sept test outcome and whether the going-concern wording is repeated. No RNS since 10 Sep announces a covenant amendment or waiver, which argues for compliance and is why this is sized small. The money bought fleet for mobilising contracts and the ProService channel, and both are corroborated by the revenue growth to July, so this is not distress financing.

baseline_tension: The priced lean (+0.06) and the 20-day run-up (+0.9%) are near-neutral, while the 60-day run-up (-25%) shows the low-end guide is already in the price. The findings lean slightly negative (-0.7) against that heavy de-rating, which is why p_up is held at 46 rather than lower.
language_note: The domestic RNS record (Investegate) carried the decisive facts: the issuer-confirmed date, the absence of any pre-close update this year, the Sept-2026 covenant reversion and the going-concern emphasis of matter in the FY26 statement, and the counterparty ProService's 'ahead of management expectations' wording. The English wire and search results surfaced none of these; they returned only the 2025 interims and the April 2026 warning.
The regional trade press (Construction Enquirer, International Rental News) carried only older FY26 coverage, nothing the RNS did not.
lessons_applied: 'Macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until the company or a counterparty has said it': the PMI/H2-weighting guidance finding was cut from -1.0 to -0.8. It stays filed because it rests partly on the company's own H2-weighting statement.

'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': the ProService counterparty finding was cut from +0.4 to +0.3, because Speedy's own AGM statement two days later had already called that trading encouraging.

'The move is in the guide' and 'size the move on what is new': abs_move_pct confirmed at 8 (numbers not pre-released, guidance change plausible, thin turnover, geared equity). Neither the reaction history nor sign uncertainty shrank it.

'Financing is a question': asked what the debt bought (fleet for mobilising contracts and the ProService channel, corroborated by revenue growth to July), so the covenant finding stays small at -0.5 with a wide range rather than being sized as distress.
